Main charitable entity types: ONGs under Lei n.º 8/2012: associações, fundações e instituições de direito privado sem fins lucrativos (art. 2), constituted per the general law (Código Civil 1966); classes: nacionais, estrangeiras, internacionais (art. 6); optional ONGIP (utilidade pública) chapter (arts. 19-34), with tax and customs exemptions for ONGIP (art. 30); FONG-STP is the national NGO federation.
Est. cost & time: Fees: unpublished (no official fee schedule; notarial deed + registration costs vary; ONGIPs exempt per Art. 30). Time: 15-day decision (Art. 9.5) + 15-day certificate (Art. 9.6) statutory; 2-6 months practical (registry needs ≥2 yrs activity, ≥10 members, Art. 9.2)
Key local requirements: Escritura pública (notarial public deed) for constitution and amendments (art. 3.1); Registo Nacional das ONG's at DGRN, entry by despacho do Ministro da Justiça (art. 9.1, 9.5); registry open only to ONGs with effective activity, ≥2 years of existence and ≥10 members (art. 9.2); foreign NGO: admitted to activity of recognized public utility (art. 6.3); must partner with national entities in the same area (art. 13); local-staff preference (art. 11.2); filings in Portuguese.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Escritura pública (notarial deed) plus Registo Nacional entry by despacho do Ministro da Justiça (15-day statutory window, art. 9.5-9.6); registry eligibility requires ≥2 years activity and ≥10 members (art. 9.2); home-country gazette extract (art. 9.3) or certified constitutive act (art. 9.4); parceria with national entities (art. 13); very small under-resourced administration; Portuguese filings
Notes: Verified against Lei n.º 8/2012 full text (DAN05-IIS, 28-05-2012, 41 articles). Prior 'declaration' framing was wrong: art. 3.1 requires escritura pública; no prior 'agrement' exists in the law. Registry entry by Minister of Justice despacho (15-day statutory window). Foreign founders face no nationality bar (art. 6.3), but must provide home-country gazette extract of the constitutive act (art. 9.3) or a certified constitutive act where no such publication exists (art. 9.4). Very small, under-resourced administration; Portuguese filings. | few public sources, details thin
